newsitem.title: USA: INTERVIEW - Fibreboard CEO sees buying spree in 1997.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Fibreboard CEO sees buying spree in 1997.

text.p: Fibreboard Corp plans to make large acquisitions in 1997 and has up to $300 million to finance its buying spree, Chief Executive Officer John Roach said.
"We are probably as active as we have ever been right now and we are looking at some very large, interesting opportunities," Roach said in an interview.

The Dallas-based building products firm earlier announced it had completed the sale of its ski resorts division for about $126 million. After-tax cash proceeds from the sale of the resorts to Booth Creek Inc were about $92 million.
Roach said the sale leaves Fibreboard with $50 million of cash in the bank, a $200 million credit line and the option to extend that line to finance its expansion.
"We have easily available $300 million for acquisitions in 1997. That doesn't mean we'll spend it all, but we are certainly looking for opportunities to invest up to that amount," he said.
He said the potential targets are all building products companies. "They are all in specialist niches; a couple are public and a couple are private."
Roach said the sale of Fibreboard's Resort Group would reduce earnings per share by $0.20-$0.25 in the last three months of 1996 and $0.55-$0.65 in the first quarter of 1997.
Its overall negative impact on 1997 earnings per share would be $0.40-0.45, but Roach said the acquisitions now made possible by the sale would largely make up for the Resort Group's lost earnings.

"Our objective clearly is to replace it, and I have absolutely no doubt we will make a sizable acqusition or two during 1997," he said, adding that the effect on earnings per share would depend on the timing of any acquisitions.
Divesting its three California ski resorts was central to Fibreboard's strategy of focusing all its energies on its core building products business.
Roach said he expected rapid internal growth and a steady rise in Fibreboard's market share of the vinyl siding business, which now accounts for about 80 percent of revenues.

He said Fibreboard currently produces about 330 million square feet of vinyl siding per year but that output would rise to 430-440 million square feet in 1997, close to 500 million square feet in 1998 and 600-700 million square feet by the end of the decade.

"Our current businesses clearly have the momentum to grow past the $700 million range (of annual revenues) within a few years ... If we utilize our financial resources to acquire businesses, that will easily bring $300-$400 million of revenues, so we expect to be at a $1 billion level within two or three years and clearly by the end of the decade," Roach said.

He said such growth would generate earnings per share of between $4 and $5 by the end of the decade. "That is a very realistic target and the precise timing of that will depend on our acquisition program."
Prior to the sale of the Resort Group, the First Call consensus of analysts' estimates put Fibreboard's 1996 earnings per share at $2.94.
The company's shares were 2-1/8 lower at 32-1/8 in late trading on the American Stock Exchange, after earlier dropping as low as 30-1/2.
